newsitem.title: CROATIA: Italian firms want to build Croatian roads - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italian firms want to build Croatian roads - paper.

text.p: Italian firms are interested in contracts to build some of 3,000 km new roads in Croatia, Croatian daily newspaper Slobodna Dalmacija reported in the week-end edition.

It said representatives of the association of private industrialists who last Friday met Croatia's Reconstruction and Development Minister, Jure Radic, said they were interested in building a coastal road along the northern Adriatic.
Another project the Italians had their eye on was a highway between capital Zagreb and the central Dalmatian port of Split.
Croatia still has to invite bids for concessions for these two important sections of its proposed new road network.

An agreement with a construction firm Astaldi was already in the works for a key 100 km stretch of the highway between Zagreb and the Hungarian border to link Croatia with Central Europe, Slobodna Dalmacija said, but it mentioned no figures.

Radic and Italy's Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni were said to have discussed joint plans for the construction of hydro-electric and thermal power plants in the former Yugoslav republic and development of the Adriatic basin.
